family: unary visit counter fed to an irregular word
summary: Mirror image of 1RB1RA_0LC0RF_1LD1LC_1RE1LB_---0RA_1RF0RD started in another state (tables: exact). It halts iff the chaotic word W eats the whole run of 1s (Lean); no halt in 3·10<sup>9</sup> visits (8.6·10<sup>18</sup> steps), W eats at most 18 cells in a visit.
title: What is known about 1RB1RA_1LC1RE_---0LD_1LE1LD_0RA0LF_1LF0LB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RA_1LC1RE_---0LD_1LE1LD_0RA0LF_1LF0LB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. This machine is the mirror image of 1RB1RA_0LC0RF_1LD1LC_1RE1LB_---0RA_1RF0RD with its states renamed, started in another state (an exact comparison of the two tables). The two runs stay in step: the same irregular word W next to a run of 1s that counts the visits, this machine's run one cell shorter.

It halts only if W eats the whole run between two visits (a Lean theorem). An exact simulation that keeps the run as a number followed it for 3·10<sup>9</sup> visits (8.6·10<sup>18</sup> steps): the run gains 0.96 cells a visit and W never eats more than 18 cells at once. W behaves like a small chaotic engine with exponential tails, so a halt is extremely unlikely, but there is no proof.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (C0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: For every length n of the run and any tape around it: L A> 1^n R reaches L 1^n A> R; L 1^n D> 1 R reaches L D> 1 1^n R. These are the moves the head makes across the long uniform stretches of the tape.

claims.title: Mirror image of a sibling
claims.text: Swapping L and R and renaming the states A,B,C,D,E,F to C,D,E,A,B,F turns this table into the table of 1RB1RA_0LC0RF_1LD1LC_1RE1LB_---0RA_1RF0RD, entry by entry (an exact comparison by script). So this machine from blank tape is the mirror image of the sibling started in its state C.

claims.title: The two runs stay in step
claims.text: At every visit of the far end the irregular word W is the same in both machines (mirrored) and this machine's run of 1s is one cell shorter: checked cell for cell at the first visits, and by W's length and the depth and eating statistics at 3·10<sup>7</sup> visits.

claims.title: No halt in 3·10<sup>7</sup> visits
claims.text: The simulator that keeps the run as a number (checked against its cell-by-cell mode) runs 30,000,000 visits = 864,573,434,721,961 steps without a halt; the run is then 28,822,305 cells and W 1,178,039.

claims.title: No halt in 3·10<sup>9</sup> visits
claims.text: The same exact run with W kept in a ring buffer (only the cells near the run are read again) went 3·109 visits = 8.6·1018 steps without a halt. It agrees with c/runsim.c on every line both print.

claims.title: A chaotic engine with exponential tails
claims.text: An excursion reads only the cells of W next to the run, with an exponential tail in depth (each further 128 cells about 4.7 times rarer); the deepest grows like the logarithm of the visits (1,582 cells by 3·10<sup>9</sup> visits). The 160 cells next to the run never repeat in 2·10<sup>6</sup> visits, and the frozen trail W leaves behind has about half a bit of entropy per cell. Cells eaten per excursion have an exponential tail too (record 18 by 3·10<sup>9</sup> visits).

claims.title: A halt needs blank tape left of the head
claims.text: A closed tape language from windows of 3 cells covers the run from blank tape; in it the halting transition C0 can fire only with blank tape left of the head. So the machine halts from blank tape iff C reads a 0 with nothing but blank tape on its left, that is, iff W eats the whole run of 1s.

claims.title: No halt in the first 3.33×10<sup>11</sup> steps (region-memo accelerator)
claims.text: The region-memo accelerator tools/py/bbtools/regaccel.py ran with blocks of 4 cells, from blank tape for 600 seconds and reached step 3.33×1011 without a halt. It keeps the tape run-length coded and, for each stretch of tape from the left end, a macro (the run until the head first leaves that stretch) computed by a symbolic run of the machine with the long runs as variables; a macro is used only when the linear inequalities its symbolic run assumed hold, otherwise the stretch is run again by the same recursion. So the run is exact, step count included. Check: 85 configurations of this run (every time the head faced blank tape on the right, up to 2×109 steps) agree cell for cell with a direct run (tools/py/regcheck.py). This is a bounded run and says nothing about later steps.

claims.title: It almost certainly never halts
claims.text: A halt at visit v needs one excursion to eat about 0.96·v cells; the number eaten has an exponential tail (record 18 cells in 3·10<sup>9</sup> visits), so the chance is of the order 10<sup>-v/2</sup>.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. W behaves as a chaotic engine (positive entropy, no period); a proof needs a bound on what one excursion can eat that holds for every W the machine can make.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1RA_0LC0RF_1LD1LC_1RE1LB_---0RA_1RF0RD up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows, but almost certainly not. This machine is the mirror image of another holdout, started in a different state. Next to a long run of 1s that counts its visits sits a small chaotic engine; the machine halts only if the engine eats the whole run in one go. An exact shortcut simulation followed it for 8.6·10<sup>18</sup> steps without a halt.

facts.text: Same table as 1RB1RA_0LC0RF_1LD1LC_1RE1LB_---0RA_1RF0RD, reflected and renamed.
No halt in 3·10<sup>9</sup> visits (exact simulation, the run as a number).
Crossing the block of 1s both ways, proved for every length.
Lean: it halts iff C reads a 0 with blank tape on its left.

sections.heading: A machine and its mirror twin
html: Take this machine's table, swap left and right everywhere, and rename the states (A,B,C,D,E,F become C,D,E,A,B,F). You get exactly the table of another holdout, 1RB1RA_0LC0RF_1LD1LC_1RE1LB_---0RA_1RF0RD. So the two are the same machine seen in a mirror, only started in different states.

Both keep a long run of 1s (a counter of the visits to the end of the tape) next to a small, messy word W where all the work happens. W cannot tell how long the run is: the head either crosses the whole run and adds a 1, or nibbles at its near end. Because of that the two machines stay in step: at every visit their words W are the same cell for cell, and this machine's run is exactly one cell shorter than its twin's.

The machine stops only if W eats the whole run between two visits. In thirty million visits W never ate more than 14 cells at once, while the run grew to 28.8 million cells. Larger bites get rarer very fast, so a halt is not expected; but W looks random, and nobody can prove it.

sections.heading: A chaotic engine next to the run
html: Why does no repeating pattern show up, whatever block size a simulator uses? Because the word W next to the run is not a counter or any other regular structure. It behaves like a small chaotic engine: each excursion of the head reads a few dozen to a few hundred cells of W next to the run, rewrites them, sometimes eats a few cells of the run, and goes back. The engine drifts slowly into the run (0.04 cells a visit) and leaves behind a frozen trail that is never read again.

How deep the head goes. The depth of an excursion has an exponential tail: every further 128 cells is about 4.7 times rarer. So there is no wall, only a steep slope, and the deepest excursion grows like the logarithm of the number of visits (1,202 cells by 3·107 visits, 1,582 by 3·109).

No repetition, and real randomness. The 160 cells next to the run never took the same value twice in two million visits. The trail behind has about half a bit of information per cell (59% ones, runs of 0s at most 2 long). A counter, a substitution word or any other rigid structure would have zero entropy; this one does not.

How much one excursion eats. Most excursions eat 0 or 1 cell of the run (and about half give one back, when a 1 of W joins the run). Large bites are exponentially rare, about ten to forty times rarer for every 2 more cells (first 108 visits):

What a halt would take. A halt needs one excursion to eat the whole run (proved in Lean: the machine halts iff state C reads a 0 with only blank tape on its left). After v visits the run holds about 0.96·v cells, and the biggest bite ever seen is 18 cells. On these tails the chance of a halt at visit v is of the order of 10-v/2. That is why everyone expects it to run for ever; but a proof would need either a rigid description of the engine, which this chaotic behaviour rules out for now, or a bound on what one excursion can eat that holds for every W the machine can make.

sections.heading: A long block and a messy engine
html: Each sweep the head comes out of the disordered region on the right, runs left through the block of 1s, turns at the end of the tape in state E and runs back. Lean proves both crossings for every length. The block gains about one cell per visit:

stepblock of 1s
2.6·1074,748
2.2·10814,358
8.7·10828,334
2·10943,506

The disordered region, about 1,500 cells of short runs at 2·109 steps (0 1 0 1 0 1 0 1 0^2 1^2 0 1^4 0 1 0 1 …), grows slowly and never repeats: its contents differed at all 45,734 visits of the left end. So it is not a small finite controller; it carries its own unbounded structure, and the halt (state C reading a 0) would have to come from there.

sections.heading: The region works like the low end of a counter
html:
Compare the region at one visit of the left end with the region at the next, starting from its far (right) end. Most of it is unchanged: only a stretch next to the big block of 1s is rewritten, like the low digits of a counter, where the lowest digits change every time and the higher ones only when a carry reaches them. In the first 3·108 steps (17,520 visits) the rewritten stretch is longer than 20 cells about half the time, longer than 80 cells one time in seven, longer than 320 cells one time in 250.

The short rewrites come from a small repertoire, for example 0101010100 → 010101011 (the block gains two cells; 3,337 times) and 01001110100 → 010011011101 (the block unchanged; 1,378 times). The long ones are different: they replace long stretches with new contents that never recur, so this is not a counter with fixed digits, and its rule is not known yet.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.512). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 32,607 cells (23,545 left of the start, 343 right), with a density of 1s of 0.972.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.
